source.title: A real-world study of immune thrombocytopenia management during the COVID-19 pandemic in the UK

extraction_metadata.scope_note: The primary article and five supplied supplements were inspected. Bibliography entries were not atomized. Comparisons remain observational and unadjusted unless the source states otherwise.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study evaluated real-world management of adults with new or relapsed immune thrombocytopenia during the COVID-19 pandemic, audited practice against UK consensus guidance, and compared the observed efficacy of first-line treatments.
The investigators conducted a national prospective observational study across 24 UK NHS hospital trusts, including 21 tertiary centres and three district hospitals.
Data collectors submitted cases through an online form with prespecified questions.
Eligible participants were older than 18 years and had new or relapsed immune thrombocytopenia during 1 March 2020 through 1 March 2021.

population.label: Adults with new or relapsed ITP during 01/03/2020-01/03/2021
inclusion_criteria: New or relapsed ITP during study period

atoms.canonical_statement: Treatment success was defined as no need for a further treatment line within 28 days.

outcome.definition: No need for a further treatment line within 28 days

atoms.canonical_statement: Platelet response was assessed by whether the platelet count exceeded 30 x10^9/L on days 7, 14, and 28.

outcome.definition: Platelet count greater than 30 x10^9/L assessed at days 7, 14, and 28

atoms.canonical_statement: Patient data were anonymised at source, and each participating centre obtained local service evaluation or audit approval.
Of 343 submitted cases, 335 were eligible for analysis and eight were excluded because age was under 18 years.

population.label: Eligible analysis cohort
exclusion_criteria: Eight submitted cases excluded for age <18 years

atoms.canonical_statement: The eligible cohort had a median age of 57 years with range 18 to 98, and 161 of 335 participants were male.
The study reported 76 secondary ITP cases, described as 22.3% of the 335-patient eligible cohort.
Among 335 eligible cases, 213 were new diagnoses and 122 were relapses.
Among 122 relapses, 50 patients were receiving maintenance therapy at relapse; among 44 on single maintenance therapy, 29 were receiving a TPO-RA.
The median platelet count at diagnosis was 7 x10^9/L with range 0 to 71, and treatment was commenced in 318 of 335 eligible cases.
Among 243 patients tested for COVID-19 at ITP diagnosis, 23 tested positive, corresponding to 9.5%.

population.label: Patients tested for COVID-19 at ITP diagnosis

atoms.canonical_statement: Using the eligible analysis denominator, 23 of 335 patients had a positive COVID-19 test, reported as 6.9%.
Among the 23 COVID-19-positive patients, the median time from onset of COVID-19 symptoms to ITP diagnosis was 12.5 days with range 2 to 60 days.

concept.text: Time from COVID-19 symptom onset to ITP diagnosis

atoms.canonical_statement: Thirteen of 23 COVID-19-positive patients required inpatient admission.
Five of 23 COVID-19-positive patients required intubation for ventilation.
Four COVID-19-positive patients were on maintenance ITP therapy; all four were receiving mycophenolate, all were admitted, and two required intubation.

population.label: COVID-19-positive patients on maintenance ITP therapy

atoms.canonical_statement: Fourteen of 76 secondary ITP cases were attributed to COVID-19 vaccination, and presentation occurred a median 24 days after vaccination with range 2 to 35 days.
Among 318 treated patients, 189 received corticosteroids as induction treatment.
Among 318 treated patients, 47 received a TPO-RA as induction treatment.
Among 318 treated patients, 51 received IVIG as induction treatment.

The remaining induction strategies were grouped as other treatments, with 31 patients in the baseline table and 17 listed under other treatment strategies in Table II, reflecting different analysis groupings and missing outcomes.

Corticosteroids and other treatments were used mainly in new diagnoses, whereas TPO-RA was used mainly in relapsed disease; the source reports 76.2% new diagnoses in the corticosteroid group, 71% in other treatments, and 80.1% relapsed disease in the TPO-RA group.
Low platelet count below 20 x10^9/L was an indication for treatment in 148 of 318 treated cases.

atoms.canonical_statement: Thrombotic complications were reported in 11 of 189 patients receiving Corticosteroids as induction treatment (5.8%).
Thrombotic complications were reported in 1 of 47 patients receiving TPO-RA as induction treatment (2.1%).
Thrombotic complications were reported in 1 of 51 patients receiving IVIG as induction treatment (2.0%).
The prose reports thrombosis in 1 of 31 patients receiving no treatment, or 3.2%.
Across the management episode, 251 of 335 eligible patients received corticosteroids at some point, corresponding to 74.9%.

concept.text: Any corticosteroid exposure during ITP episode

atoms.canonical_statement: Steroid weaning began within 7 days in 99 of 251 corticosteroid-exposed cases.
Steroid weaning began during days 8 to 14 in 74 of 251 corticosteroid-exposed cases.
Steroid weaning began after more than 15 days in 49 of 251 corticosteroid-exposed cases.
Table S1 reports median platelet counts at diagnosis of 6 x10^9/L in the corticosteroid group, 14 x10^9/L in the TPO-RA group, 6 x10^9/L in the IVIG group, and 5 x10^9/L in other treatments.

Table S1 reports secondary ITP as 50/189 in the corticosteroid group, 3/47 in the TPO-RA group, 15/25 in the IVIG column, and 6/31 in other treatments; the IVIG denominator of 25 is not explained by the column header N=51.

Supplementary Table S3 lists 76 secondary ITP diagnoses; the most frequent listed categories include COVID vaccination 14, SLE 8, low-grade B-cell lymphoma 5, antiphospholipid syndrome 4, COVID-19 infection 4, alemtuzumab 3, and HIV 3.

Figure S1 shows 92 of 189 corticosteroid-treated patients as first-line treatment successes (48.7%) and separately identifies eight patients with unknown first-line outcome; Table II instead calculates success as 92/181 (50.8%) after excluding those missing outcomes.
Figure S1 shows that after corticosteroid first-line failure, 23 of 30 patients treated with TPO-RA as second line did not proceed to third-line treatment, or 76.7%.

concept.text: No third-line treatment after second-line therapy

atoms.canonical_statement: Figure S1 shows treatment success in 13 of 36 patients receiving IVIG as second-line treatment after corticosteroid failure, or 36.1%.

Figure S2 plots monthly ITP cases from January 2020 through April 2021; the bars rise through late 2020, are highest around February 2021, and then fall sharply by April 2021. Exact values are not printed on the bars.
The authors concluded that TPO-RA can be a safe and effective treatment choice for newly diagnosed or relapsed ITP and that corticosteroid efficacy appeared inferior to TPO-RA in this cohort.
The authors stated that clinical trials are needed to confirm the benefits of TPO-RA as first-line agents for ITP.
The authors described the multicentre professional-network approach as a way to collect a representative and timely national snapshot of ITP practice.
The study used lack of second-line therapy as a real-world success outcome, and the authors noted that this may have penalised IVIG when used alone as first-line treatment.
Time to platelet count above 30 x10^9/L may have followed one or more lines of treatment, so that response timing cannot always be attributed to the initial treatment.
The authors acknowledged potential biases inherent in the real-world study design, while noting prospective data collection, a predefined form, and focus on objective outcomes as mitigation steps.
Treatment groups differed in disease status and secondary ITP frequency, and the article reports unadjusted success rates without randomized assignment or an adjusted comparative model.
The study received funding from the Oxford Centre for Haematology Research.
The authors disclosed no conflicts of interest.

Table I labels the overall column n=343 and reports 23/343 positive COVID-19 tests, while the Results section defines the eligible cohort as n=335 and separately reports 23/335 overall; the tested subgroup denominator is 243.
Table I prints post-COVID-19 vaccination as 0/3 (100%) in the maintenance-therapy column, which is arithmetically inconsistent with the numerator and denominator.

Table II reports fourth-line treatment in 33/172 corticosteroid cases (19.2%) even though the overall fourth-line row is 20/295 (6.8%), and the prednisolone and dexamethasone fourth-line subrows sum to 10 cases.

The Table II thrombosis footnote says there were seven venous thromboses but then enumerates three deep vein thromboses, four pulmonary embolisms, one portal vein thrombosis, and one sinus venous thrombosis, which totals nine venous events.
The Results prose states that 23/30 second-line TPO-RA cases avoided third-line treatment at 76.1%, whereas Figure S1 prints 23/30 as 76.7%.

The article and Table S1 report 76/335 secondary ITP as 22.3%, although that fraction is approximately 22.7%; Table S1 also contains a drug-induced row of 6/78 despite the stated secondary-ITP total of 76.
